name: SLUE
description: Progress in speech processing has been facilitated by shared datasets and benchmarks. Historically these have focused on automatic speech recognition (ASR), speaker identification, or other lower-level tasks. Interest has been growing in higher-level spoken language understanding tasks, including using end-to-end models, but there are fewer annotated datasets for such tasks. At the same time, recent work shows the possibility of pre-training generic representations and then fine-tuning for several tasks using relatively little labeled data. We propose to create a suite of benchmark tasks for Spoken Language Understanding Evaluation (SLUE) consisting of limited-size labeled training sets and corresponding evaluation sets. This resource would allow the research community to track progress, evaluate pre-trained representations for higher-level tasks, and study open questions such as the utility of pipeline versus end-to-end approaches. We present the first phase of the SLUE benchmark suit
typical_sota_score: varies by task; roughly 75–95% depending on subtask (intent accuracy often 85–95%, slot-filling F1 often 75–90%)
reputation: A well-known benchmark suite in spoken language understanding research, used to compare end-to-end and pipeline approaches.
notes: Speech benchmark suite with relatively small labeled training sets; performance varies by subtask and dataset, and results can be sensitive to pretraining and fine-tuning setup.
